questions.stem: A user downloads software for macOS and receives a file with a .dmg extension. What should the user do to install the software?

choices.text: Run it directly like an .exe file
Double-click to mount it as a virtual drive, then run the installer inside
Extract it with Archive Utility, then run setup
Rename it to .pkg before opening

questions.explanation: A .dmg is an Apple disk image. Double-clicking mounts it in Finder as a virtual drive. The user then typically drags the .app to Applications or runs a .pkg inside the image.
questions.trap: DMGs are not executables and cannot be renamed to .pkg - they serve different purposes.

questions.stem: A macOS user wants to remove an application. There is no Uninstall option in the app. What is the correct procedure?

choices.text: Use Control Panel > Programs and Features to uninstall
Open Terminal and run rm -rf /Applications/AppName
Drag the .app file from the Applications folder to the Trash
Disable the app in System Preferences > Users and Groups

questions.explanation: Most macOS apps are self-contained bundles. Dragging the .app to Trash removes the application and all its bundled files. There is no Programs and Features equivalent.
questions.trap: Control Panel does not exist on macOS. Terminal rm -rf works but is not the standard user-facing procedure.

questions.stem: A macOS administrator notices the OS version on a device shows '14.1.1a'. What does the letter suffix indicate?

choices.text: A beta pre-release version is installed
A Rapid Security Response update has been applied
The system is in developer mode
A hardware-specific firmware patch was applied

questions.explanation: A letter appended to the macOS version number (e.g., 14.1.1a) indicates a Rapid Security Response (RSR) update has been applied - an emergency critical security patch pushed immediately by Apple.
questions.trap: Beta versions have a different designation in the software update system, not a letter suffix on the release version.

questions.stem: Which macOS feature is equivalent to Windows BitLocker?

choices.text: Keychain
FileVault
Time Machine
Disk Utility

questions.explanation: FileVault provides full disk encryption on macOS, encrypting the entire drive using the login password or iCloud credentials - directly analogous to Windows BitLocker.
questions.trap: Keychain encrypts stored credentials, not the disk. Disk Utility manages partitions but does not provide encryption.

questions.stem: A macOS application has stopped responding. Which keystroke opens the Force Quit window?

choices.text: Command+Option+Delete
Command+Option+Escape
Control+Alt+Delete
Command+Shift+Escape

questions.explanation: Command+Option+Escape opens the Force Quit Applications window, showing all running apps. The user can select the unresponsive app and click Force Quit.
questions.trap: Control+Alt+Delete is the Windows equivalent. Command+Option+Delete is not a system shortcut.

questions.stem: A user asks how to search for a file across their entire macOS system. What is the fastest built-in method?

choices.text: Open Finder and select File > Find
Press Command+Space to open Spotlight
Open Terminal and run find /
Open Disk Utility and search the volume

questions.explanation: Spotlight (Command+Space) is macOS's system-wide search that instantly searches apps, documents, images, contacts, and more.
questions.trap: Finder search works but is scoped to what is visible. Spotlight is the system-wide equivalent of Windows Search.

questions.stem: Match each macOS feature to its Windows equivalent.
questions.explanation: Cross-platform equivalents are a favorite exam pattern. Know the macOS side and its Windows counterpart for each.

questions.stem: An IT department deploys Apple devices for corporate users and wants single sign-on using existing Active Directory credentials. Which Apple feature enables this?

choices.text: iCloud with a personal Apple ID
Managed Apple ID via Apple Business Manager
Keychain integration with LDAP
FileVault with institutional recovery key

questions.explanation: Managed Apple IDs are created and managed through Apple Business Manager, which integrates with Active Directory to allow users to authenticate with their existing corporate credentials.
questions.trap: Personal Apple IDs cannot integrate with AD. Keychain stores credentials but does not federate with AD.

questions.stem: Which of the following are TRUE about macOS Time Machine? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Creates hourly backups for the past 24 hours
Creates daily backups for the past month
Stores backups exclusively in iCloud
Deletes oldest backups automatically when the volume fills

questions.explanation: Time Machine backs up hourly/daily/weekly to a local or network volume - not exclusively to iCloud. iCloud is a separate service.
questions.trap: (c) Time Machine uses a local drive or network volume, NOT iCloud. iCloud backup is a separate Apple feature.
